compareDisposition.rationale: The curator examined Moses returns toward Egypt beside God calls Moses at the bush; The name and commission are given; Signs answer Moses’ objections; Moses and Aaron gather Israel. Those passages share its exodus evidence group or Scripture movement, but none supplies a distinct two-source relationship stronger than the accepted comparisons already carrying this topic.

context.body: The passage reports the threat, Zipporah’s action, her words, and the release, but does not add an explanation of the encounter.
context.label: What remains unstated

observations.body: Moses leaves Midian with his wife, sons, donkey, and God’s rod to return toward Egypt.
observations.label: Return begins

observations.body: Before the lodging place, Israel is called the LORD’s son and firstborn, and Pharaoh’s firstborn is threatened.
observations.label: Firstborn language

observations.body: At the lodging place, the LORD meets Moses and wants to kill him.
observations.label: A lethal meeting

observations.body: Zipporah uses a flint, circumcises her son, casts the foreskin at his feet, and speaks of a bridegroom of blood.
observations.label: Zipporah acts

observations.body: The passage says, “So he let him alone,” without explicitly naming the referents of every pronoun in the encounter.
observations.label: The threat ceases

payload.posture: Read the brief lodging-place encounter at face value, marking every named actor and every unresolved pronoun.
payload.tension: A commissioned journey toward Egypt is interrupted by a lethal encounter that ends after Zipporah acts, while key pronoun referents remain unstated.
payload.title: The journey is interrupted
